nodes.name: GS - Load Lead Record
nodes.notes: alwaysOutputData is required so a lead_id that somehow has no matching row still emits one empty item, which CODE - Check Send Eligibility below turns into a 'missing' outcome instead of silently killing the branch.

nodes.name: SWT - Check Send Eligibility
nodes.notes: Outputs 0=eligible, 1=already_sent, 2=missing, 3=extra (fallback safety net, routed the same as 'missing').

nodes.name: GS - Load Email Templates
nodes.notes: Loads template_id/subject/body rows. This is now the single source of the approved copy - CODE - Build Result Email must never hard-code subject/body text, per spec section 6.1 (Email_Templates: 'Approved subject lines and message bodies') and handover point 15.2 #10 ('explain how to change copy... without breaking workflows').

nodes.name: HTTP - Send Result Email
nodes.notes: Sends via the raw Gmail API instead of the standard Gmail node so a custom X-Client-Type/X-Client-Sheet-Id header can be set on the outgoing message - the standard Gmail node's send operation has no option to set custom headers. Response shape ({id, threadId, labelIds}) matches what the Gmail node used to return, so CODE - Record Send Result needed no changes.

nodes.name: GS - Append Activity Log (Skipped Duplicate)
nodes.notes: T15 (workflow retry must be idempotent): reached when Leads.status is already past 'New submission', meaning a result email already went out for this lead. No second email is sent.

nodes.name: GS - Append Activity Log (Lead Not Found)
nodes.notes: Logged before the failure below so the event survives even though the execution ultimately errors out.

parameters.jsCode: throw new Error(`WF-02: No Leads row found for lead_id "${$json.lead_id}". Cannot send result email - check that WF-01 upserted this lead before calling WF-02.`);

nodes.name: CODE - Fail Missing Lead Record
nodes.notes: Deliberately throws so this execution is marked failed and routes to the workflow's Error Workflow (WF-99), per spec 8.8 and the Critical severity row in 13.3.
